doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Monk's Milt Hinton memory and gigs that stand out
summary: Monk recalls Hinton falling asleep on his shoulder; they talk about the magnetism of such musicians and special gigs.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: You know everybody who met the guy had his memories. He fell asleep on my shoulder once. That’s my memory.

Yeah. I mean we were in a van going with the Statesmen of Jazz and I was riding with them. And he fell asleep on my shoulder, and I’m going [gasp] Milt Hinton. But some of those people have this magnetism to them, like you feel better after you’ve been able to just be near them.

Do you know what I mean? For those moments. And they don’t come around every day. At other times the gigs are just, well it was okay, you know. And sometimes it doesn’t sound so great. It’s okay. Or most of the time I’m playing with people, they’re good gigs. I’m very fortunate. But those gigs are like wow, those are the gigs that stand out in your brain. And it’s like pinch me, am I here? They’re the ones that are special.
